title: introduce-latency-cohorting-and-telemetry-bridge-for-per-token-cost-attribution
author: Asha Iyer
description: Motivation: long-tail latency and cost spikes are often concentrated in a small set of request cohorts (similar prompts, chains, or multi-turn patterns) but existing rollups blend them away. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a 'latency cohorting' layer that buckets requests by a lightweight signature (prompt fingerprint + sequence-length class + model-variant) and produces cohort-level token latency/cost histograms; 2) a telemetry-bridge that correlates serving spans to billing units (model shards, quantization profile, and GPU type) so cost attribution can be broken down by both request cohort and infra dimension. What changed: added a cohorting aggregator that runs as an optional stage in the router pipeline; extended span tags to include cohort_id, billing_unit, quant_profile and hw_class; introduced a new compact histogram type (reservoir-slab) for cohorted token latency and cost; added a telemetry bridge service that enriches traces with billing metadata and emits cohort+billing rollups to metrics and to the observability events index. Included a new set of dashboards (Cohorts: latency & cost explorer, Cohort SLO decomposition) and a smaller alerting surface: dynamic per-cohort SLO scaling rules and adaptive suppression for noisy low-volume cohorts. Rollout plan: feature-gated behind rollout flag obs.cohorting.enabled=false by default; staged rollout to 10% traffic, then 50%, then 100% following perf validation. Checklist: - implement cohort id and deterministic fingerprinting - add span enrichment and telemetry bridge - add reservoir-slab histogram implementation and aggregation keys - expose metrics (cohort.token_latency.pXX,p50,p90,p99, cohort.token_cost.sum,count) - add dashboards and alert rules - tests (unit + e2e with synthetic replay) - documentation updates and migration notes for Query APIs Backwards compatibility: cohorting is opt-in; spans without cohort tags continue to be indexed normally. Performance: the cohorting stage uses a bounded in-memory LRU and is optimized to avoid per-token allocations; we ran local load tests with 5000 rps where CPU overhead stayed under 3% and memory within limits. Risks & mitigations: added a watchdog that disables cohorting if reservoir allocations exceed configured thresholds; billing correlation is best-effort and falls back to existing per-request cost tags. Related: follows up on ENG-5274 (cost-attribution proto) and complements ENG-7213 (slo decomposition).

review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Can we make the fingerprint stable across restarts? Suggest storing the salt in config and falling back to a deterministic default.
Asha Iyer (author): replied: added persisted salt in router config (see aggregator.go) and documented migration implications.
Samantha Park: The reservoir implementation needs a deterministic seeding strategy for reproducible A/B comparisons.
Asha Iyer (author): replied: seeding is wired to cohort_id+namespace; added unit tests to validate determinism.
Daniel Kim: Alerting rules look noisy at low volume. Can we add an adaptive suppression window?
Asha Iyer (author): replied: added adaptive suppression and a configurable min_volume threshold; updated alert docs and dashboard annotations.

release_notes: Added optional latency cohorting and a telemetry bridge for cohort+billing cost attribution. New dashboards and adaptive per-cohort SLO rules. Opt-in via obs.cohorting.enabled and rollout flags. Notes: cohort IDs are persisted; downstream consumers should tolerate missing cohort tags for older traces.
testing_notes: Unit tests added for fingerprinting and reservoir-slab determinism. E2E synthetic replay covers long-tail scenarios and validates that cohort SLOs trigger suppression as designed. Local load tests at 5k rps measured <3% CPU overhead when enabled. Observability team validated dashboard panels and alert suppression behavior.
deployment_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: start with obs.cohorting.enabled=false. Canary: enable for 10% traffic in us-west for 48h, monitor cohort.rollup.latency and cohort.rollup.memory. If stable, expand to 50% for 72h then 100%. Watchdog will auto-disable if reservoir memory > 80% of configured budget or if trace enrichment latencies exceed 50ms p99.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on: (1) correctness and stability of fingerprinting across restarts; (2) reservoir memory/CPU characteristics under synthetic long-tail workloads; (3) alert suppression logic and the default thresholds; (4) SDK trace enrichment impact on client latency. I've included tests and dashboards to help validate these points.
authors_acknowledgement: By merging this PR we accept the telemetry schema additions and the downstream migration steps. Documentation and runbook entries have been added to the observability handbook.
